name: Ibn al-Muqarrab al-Uyuni
bio: Ali ibn al-Muqarrab al-Uyuni, born in 572 AH (1176 CE), was a poet of al-Ahsa in eastern Arabia and a member of its ruling Uyunid house; his name comes from al-Uyun, a place in Bahrain. The amir of al-Ahsa, a kinsman of his, seized his wealth and imprisoned him; once released he went to Iraq and spent some months in Baghdad, then came home and tried in vain to recover his property. In 617 AH (1220 CE) he visited Mosul, where the geographer Yaqut met him and recorded two of his lines, and where his praise of Badr al-Din Lu'lu' and other notables won him gifts and honour. Most of his verse counsels and defends the Uyunid amirs of his family, and al-Zirikli notes that the old commentary on his diwan names amirs whom the historians left out. He died in 629 AH (1232 CE), in Bahrain or at Tiwi in Oman.
